### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. corneal dystrophy-perceptive deafness syndrome  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.741)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:16438)

**Proposed mechanism:** SLC4A11 (HGNC:10600) —DISRUPTS→ Apical membrane ion/solute transport in corneal endothelium (REACT:R-HSA-72771); Apical membrane ion/solute transport in corneal endothelium (REACT:R-HSA-72771) —LEADS_TO→ Corneal dystrophy (HP:0000566); Apical membrane ion/solute transport in corneal endothelium (REACT:R-HSA-72771) —LEADS_TO→ Perceptive deafness (HP:0000418). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC4A11 disrupt apical membrane ion and solute transport in the corneal endothelium, leading to corneal dystrophy. This disruption also affects cochlear function, resulting in perceptive deafness.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in SLC4A11 associated with only one of the two phenotypes (corneal dystrophy or perceptive deafness) without the other, or a common benign variant (gnomAD allele frequency > 1%) in SLC4A11 in affected individuals. _(variant: HGNC:10600)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SLC4A11 in corneal and auditory function could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting ion transport for both conditions.

#### 2. congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy of cornea  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.719)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:16438)

**Proposed mechanism:** SLC4A11 (HGNC:16438) —DISRUPTS→ Boron transport and homeostasis (REACT:R-HSA-72700); Boron transport and homeostasis (REACT:R-HSA-72700) —LEADS_TO→ Corneal opacity (HP:0000539); Boron transport and homeostasis (REACT:R-HSA-72700) —LEADS_TO→ Macular coloboma (HP:0011247). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC4A11 disrupt boron transport and homeostasis, leading to corneal opacity in congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy and macular coloboma in familial isolated ptosis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in SLC4A11 with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease would falsify the proposed loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: rs145557573)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SLC4A11 in boron transport and its impact on ocular tissues may lead to novel therapeutic strategies for corneal dystrophies and other ocular developmental disorders by targeting pathways involved in boron homeostasis or cellular integrity.
